verifyNote: Reference guidance. Verify laws, clauses and standards for your site and country before audit use. The official site procedure always takes priority.

activities.title: Sandblasting and Painting
activities.summary: Abrasive blasting and spray painting or coating of steel and structures.

where_first: Check containment, ventilation and exhaust
Check the blast operator's air-fed helmet, breathing air quality and hose
Check the abrasive type (never silica sand) and the paint SDS
Check the exclusion zone, signs and hose coupling whip checks
hidden_hazards: Respirable crystalline silica from the surface or abrasive
Lead or chromate in old paint
Static discharge igniting solvent vapour during spraying
Hose connection failure whipping at pressure
Dust clouds hiding trip hazards and other workers
protect_first: Other workers who enter the dust cloud

elimination: Use pre-coated materials or shop priming
substitution: Use low-dust abrasives, water blasting and low-VOC paints
engineering: Enclosure and ventilation, dust extraction, dead-man valve, whip checks on couplings
administrative: Permit, breathing air quality tests, health surveillance, exclusion zone, trained operators
ppe: Air-fed helmet, blast suit, gloves, hearing protection
Respirator for spray painting with correct filter (EN 14387 / EN 149)
permits: Confined space permit where inside tanks
checklist: Hose couplings pinned with whip checks
Paint SDS read, ignition sources controlled

legal.india: Factories Act 1948; MSIHC Rules 1989 for flammable coatings (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; client coating and blasting procedures (verify)
legal.canada: Provincial OHS regulations; CSA Z94.4 (respirators); WHMIS 2015

tbt.title: Blasting: protect your lungs first
points: Only air-fed helmets in blasting, never a paper mask
Check the breathing air and the hose couplings every shift
Keep everyone else out of the dust zone
tbt.question: Who else could breathe this dust without knowing?

activities.title: Marine Mooring Operations
activities.summary: Handling mooring lines and winches when a vessel berths, shifts or departs.

where_first: Check the mooring plan, ropes and winches are inspected and in date
Check snap-back zones are marked and clear
Check crew positions, communication and the bridge to deck briefing
Check the deck is clear of oil and trip hazards
hidden_hazards: Ropes with internal damage or past retirement
Snap-back zones that look safe but are in the line of the rope
Sudden tension changes from wind, tide or swell
Rope bights around feet on deck
Poor communication between bridge, deck and shore
protect_first: People on the quay or in launches near lines

elimination: Use remote or automated mooring systems where fitted
substitution: Use ropes with higher breaking load and lower snap-back energy
engineering: Good fairleads, bitts and bollards, winch brakes and guards, marked snap-back zones
administrative: Mooring plan and risk assessment, briefing, defined roles, never stand in the bight, rope inspection records
ppe: Helmet, gloves, safety boots, lifejacket where overboard risk, high-visibility
Lifejacket or buoyancy aid where overboard risk (EN ISO 12402)
checklist: Mooring plan briefed to all crew
Deck clear of oil and obstructions

legal.india: Merchant Shipping Act 1958; DG Shipping requirements; ISM Code (verify)
legal.gulf: Flag state and port authority rules; ISM Code; OCIMF Mooring Equipment Guidelines (MEG4) (verify)
legal.canada: Canada Shipping Act 2001 and Marine Occupational Health and Safety Regulations (SOR/2010-120)
legal.usa: US Coast Guard regulations (46 CFR); OSHA 29 CFR 1915 to 1918 for shipyards, marine terminals and longshoring where applicable

tbt.title: Mooring: never stand in the bight
points: Know where the snap-back zone is and stay out
Only the person in charge gives signals
Report any damaged rope or winch before use
tbt.question: If this rope parted now, where would it fly?

activities.title: Working Aloft (Marine)
activities.summary: Working on masts, funnels, cranes and high structures on a vessel.

where_first: Check the permit to work aloft, that the bridge has been told and radar and radio aerials are isolated
Check the harness, lanyards and attachment points
Check weather and ship movement
Check tools are secured and the area below is barricaded
hidden_hazards: Radar and radio transmission at the work position
Corroded ladders or rails
Ship movement causing sudden sway
Dropped objects reaching people on deck
Sun, heat or cold stress for the person aloft

elimination: Do the work in port or from a platform or cherry picker
substitution: Use remote inspection such as a drone where possible
engineering: Fixed anchor points, rescue equipment ready, nets or barriers below
administrative: Permit to work aloft, second person on deck, communication, weather limits, rescue plan
ppe: Full body harness with two lanyards, helmet with chin strap, lifejacket where overboard risk
Full body harness with two lanyards (EN 361, EN 355)
checklist: Harness and lanyards inspected, two points of attachment
Standby person and rescue plan ready

legal.india: Merchant Shipping Act 1958; DG Shipping requirements; ISM Code (verify)
legal.gulf: Flag state rules and ISM Code; Code of Safe Working Practices for Merchant Seafarers widely used (verify)
legal.canada: Canada Shipping Act 2001 and Marine Occupational Health and Safety Regulations (SOR/2010-120)
legal.usa: US Coast Guard 46 CFR; OSHA 29 CFR 1915 for shipyards where applicable

tbt.title: Aloft: tell the bridge, switch off the radar
points: Permit and bridge permission first
Always two points of attachment
Tie every tool and keep people clear below
tbt.question: What happens to the radar while I am up there?

activities.title: Cold Room and Ammonia Refrigeration
activities.summary: Working in cold rooms and with ammonia refrigeration plant.

where_first: Check ammonia detectors, alarms and ventilation are working
Check machinery room doors, exits and emergency stop
Check eyewash, shower and breathing apparatus
Check cold room door releases and a way out from the inside
hidden_hazards: Small slow leaks from valves, flanges and relief lines
Ammonia pooling in low areas or poorly ventilated spaces
Frozen door releases trapping people inside
Ice build-up on floors and racking
Liquid ammonia trapped between valves expanding
protect_first: A worker trapped in a cold room

hazards: Explosion in a machinery room at high concentration

elimination: Use a lower charge or alternative refrigerant where suitable
substitution: Consider CO2 or other lower-toxicity systems in new designs
engineering: Ammonia detection with alarms, emergency ventilation and shutdown, inside door release and alarm
administrative: Trained operators, emergency response plan, drills, mechanical integrity inspection, cold exposure limits and rewarming breaks
ppe: Cold-protective clothing, escape respirator, goggles, insulated boots
Full face respirator with ammonia filter for escape (EN 14387 type K)
Self-contained breathing apparatus for response teams (EN 137)
permits: Hot work and line break permits for refrigeration work
checklist: Eyewash, shower and escape respirators ready
Cold room door opens from inside and alarm works
Time limits and rewarming breaks set
Trained responders and drills up to date

legal.india: Factories Act 1948; MSIHC Rules 1989; IS 660 (mechanical refrigeration safety code) (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; Civil Defence requirements for ammonia (verify)
legal.canada: CSA B52 (mechanical refrigeration code) and provincial regulations
legal.usa: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.111 (anhydrous ammonia), 1910.119 (PSM above the threshold quantity); IIAR standards

tbt.title: Ammonia: if you smell it, move out and tell someone
points: Know the escape route and the alarm
Never enter a leak area without breathing apparatus
Check that the cold room door opens from inside
tbt.question: If the lights failed now, could everyone get out of this room?

typical: Cold room door will not open inside

activities.title: Manual Handling and Racking
activities.summary: Lifting and moving loads by hand and storing goods on racking.

where_first: Check the load weight, shape and the route
Check racking for damage, bent uprights, missing beams and load notices
Check pallets and load stability
Check mechanical aids available (trolleys, hoists, lift assists)
hidden_hazards: Forklift damage to uprights that nobody reported
Overloaded beam levels or poor quality pallets
Repetitive strain from small loads handled many times
Slippery floors near docks
Stacking too high close to sprinklers
protect_first: Workers under or beside loaded racking

elimination: Remove handling by conveyors or direct delivery
substitution: Use smaller packages or lighter containers
engineering: Lifting aids, adjustable work heights, rack protectors, safe load notices, dock edge protection
administrative: Lifting technique training, team lifts, job rotation, racking inspections by a competent person, damage reporting

ppe: High-visibility clothing in traffic areas (EN ISO 20471)
checklist: Load weight known and within the limit
Racking free of damage with load notices

legal.india: Factories Act 1948 s.34 (excessive weights) and state rules (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; ISO 11228 and EN 15512 (racking) commonly specified (verify)
legal.canada: Provincial OHS regulations on musculoskeletal injury prevention
legal.usa: OSHA General Duty Clause; 29 CFR 1910.176 (handling materials)

tbt.title: Lifting by hand: use your head, not your back
points: Test the weight first and use a trolley when you can
Report any damaged racking and keep clear of it
Ask for help with long or heavy loads
tbt.question: What could we change so nobody has to lift this?

typical: Heavy load lifted by one person

activities.title: Line Breaking and Intrusive Maintenance
activities.summary: Opening pipes, flanges and equipment that may contain hydrocarbons or other hazardous fluids.

where_first: Check the isolation plan: positive isolation, depressurise, drain, purge and verify
Check the line contents and the SDS
Check the permit, gas test and ignition source control
Check emergency response, escape route and wind direction
hidden_hazards: Trapped pressure or liquid between valves
Residual hydrocarbons and H2S in dead legs
Wrong line opened because of labelling errors
Static electricity during draining
Wind carrying vapour to ignition sources or people

elimination: Avoid breaking containment through design (double block and bleed, spool pieces)
substitution: Use approved alternatives such as hot tapping under a strict procedure
engineering: Double block and bleed or blinds, vent and drain points, gas detection, drip trays
administrative: Line break permit, isolation certificate, supervised depressurising with gauges, controlled bolt loosening, rescue and fire plan
ppe: Flame-resistant coverall, chemical gloves, face shield, gas detector, escape set
Escape breathing apparatus where H2S is possible (EN 13794)
checklist: Isolation verified by a second competent person
Pressure gauge reads zero at the break point
Line drained and purged as planned
Right line confirmed against the isolation list
Gas test done and ignition sources controlled
Wind direction and escape route known

legal.india: Factories Act 1948 Chapter IVA; MSIHC Rules 1989 (verify)
legal.gulf: ADNOC and Aramco process isolation and permit standards (client documents) and UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020 (verify)
legal.canada: Provincial regulations and CSA Z767 (process safety management)

tbt.title: Line break: assume it is full until proven empty
points: Check the isolation and the gauge before opening
Open slowly and stand clear of the first release
Know the wind direction and your escape route
tbt.question: How do we know this line is really isolated and empty?

activities.title: H2S and Toxic Gas Hazards
activities.summary: Working where hydrogen sulfide or other toxic gases may be present.

where_first: Check personal and area gas detectors: calibration and bump test
Check wind socks and the upwind muster point
Check escape breathing apparatus or SCBA and who is trained
Check alarm levels and the emergency plan
hidden_hazards: H2S is heavier than air and collects in low areas and trenches
Smell fades at higher concentrations, so do not rely on your nose
Sudden release from sludge, tanks or sour lines
A rescuer becomes a second victim
Wind shifts that change the safe direction
protect_first: Anyone who collapses in the area
Workers alone or in low spots

hazards: Collapse and death at high concentrations

elimination: Remove exposure by remote operation and closed systems
substitution: Use closed sampling instead of open sampling
engineering: Fixed gas detection and alarms, ventilation, closed drains
administrative: H2S awareness training, buddy system, permit and gas testing, wind direction signs, drills
ppe: Personal H2S monitor, escape set, SCBA for rescue
Personal H2S detector worn at breathing height
checklist: Wind sock visible, upwind muster known
Escape sets and SCBA available and checked
Alarm levels set by site standard understood
Rescue plan and trained rescuers ready
Drill done in the last 6 months

legal.india: Factories Act 1948 s.36 and Chapter IVA (verify)
legal.gulf: ADNOC and Aramco H2S standards and contingency requirements (client documents) (verify)
legal.canada: Provincial energy and OHS rules (for example Alberta OHS Code and Alberta Energy Regulator requirements); CSA Z1006
legal.usa: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1000 Table Z-2 (hydrogen sulfide ceiling limit); API RP 54 and API RP 49

tbt.title: H2S: when the alarm sounds, go upwind
points: Never trust your nose. Trust the detector
Move to the upwind muster point and help others on the way
Do not run in to rescue without breathing apparatus
tbt.question: Which way is upwind from where I am standing?

typical: No wind sock or muster point

activities.title: Heat Stress in Outdoor Work
activities.summary: Working outdoors or in hot areas where heat illness can happen.

where_first: Check the heat index or WBGT and the forecast for the shift
Check shade, a cool rest area and drinking water within easy reach
Check workers new to the heat or returning from leave (acclimatisation)
Check the buddy system and emergency plan
hidden_hazards: Heat stress builds during the shift and often peaks after lunch
Workers hide symptoms for fear of losing work or pay
Dehydration from tea and coffee instead of water
Dark PPE and enclosed spaces raise body heat
Humid heat is dangerous even when the number looks lower
protect_first: Anyone with confusion, hot dry skin or collapse (emergency)

elimination: Reschedule heavy work to cooler hours
substitution: Use mechanical aids to reduce effort
engineering: Shade, fans, misting, cooled rest areas, reflective covers
administrative: Acclimatise over 5 to 7 days, work-rest cycles, water and electrolytes, buddy checks, midday work ban where law requires, heat illness first aid training
ppe: Light breathable clothing, cooling vests, neck and sun cover
Helmet with neck and sun cover (EN 397)
Cooling vests or neck wraps where provided
Sun protection: hat, sunglasses (EN 166 or EN ISO 12312-1), sunscreen
High-visibility clothing in lighter fabric (EN ISO 20471)
checklist: Heat index or WBGT checked and level noted
Shade and cool rest area available
Cool drinking water close and used
Buddy checks and emergency plan known
Midday work ban respected where applicable

legal.india: Factories Act 1948 s.13 (ventilation and temperature) and state rules; OSH Code 2020; state heat advisories (verify)
legal.gulf: National midday work ban in summer: UAE 15 June to 15 September 12:30 to 15:00; Saudi Arabia 15 June to 15 September 12:00 to 15:00; Qatar 1 June to 15 September 10:00 to 15:30 (verify current year notices)
legal.canada: Provincial OHS general duty and heat stress provisions; ACGIH TLV for heat stress
legal.usa: OSHA General Duty Clause; NIOSH criteria for heat; state rules such as Cal/OSHA Section 3395

tbt.title: Heat: water, shade, rest, and look after your partner
points: Drink a cup of water every 15 to 20 minutes, even if not thirsty
Dizziness, confusion or stopping sweating means stop and call for help
Check your partner. Heat stroke is an emergency
tbt.question: Who on our team is new to this heat today?

typical: No drinking water at work area

activities.title: Cold Stress and Winter Work
activities.summary: Working outdoors or in cold stores in low temperatures, snow and ice.

where_first: Check the wind chill and forecast
Check warm rest areas and warm drinks
Check footing: ice, snow and black ice on routes
Check vehicles and equipment are winter ready
hidden_hazards: Wind chill makes real risk far worse than the air temperature
Wet clothing causes fast heat loss
Early signs (shivering, clumsiness, slurred speech) are missed
Black ice on routes that look just wet
Metal tools and surfaces cause cold contact injury
protect_first: Lone workers and drivers in remote areas

hazards: Carbon monoxide from heaters in enclosed spaces

elimination: Postpone non-urgent outdoor work in extreme cold
substitution: Move tasks indoors or under heated shelter
engineering: Heated shelters, wind breaks, de-icing, anti-slip surfaces
administrative: Work-warm-up schedule by wind chill, buddy checks, symptom training, safe heater use, winter driving rules
ppe: Layered insulated clothing, insulated waterproof boots and gloves, face and neck cover, ice cleats
Insulated waterproof boots (EN ISO 20345 CI WR)
permits: Winter road and site ice management plan
checklist: Warm shelter and warm drinks available
Buddy checks and warm-up breaks set
Vehicles winter ready with emergency kit

legal.india: Not usually a main hazard in India; Factories Act 1948 general duties apply (verify)
legal.gulf: Not usually a main hazard in the Gulf; UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020 general duties apply (verify)
legal.canada: Provincial OHS regulations on thermal exposure (for example WorkSafeBC OHS Regulation Part 7); ACGIH TLV for cold stress
legal.usa: OSHA General Duty Clause; NIOSH guidance on cold stress

tbt.title: Cold: stay dry, stay warm, watch your partner
points: Wet clothes lose heat fast. Change them
Shivering, clumsy hands or slurred speech means get warm now
Check ice on walkways before you carry anything
tbt.question: Where is our nearest warm shelter and how long to reach it?

typical: Worker in wet clothing in cold

activities.title: Mobile Plant and Site Traffic
activities.summary: Controlling vehicles, mobile plant and pedestrians on site.

where_first: Check the traffic management plan and the separation of people and vehicles
Check reversing alarms, cameras and banksmen
Check blind spots, speed limits and signs
Check pedestrian crossings and lighting
hidden_hazards: Blind spots larger than drivers expect
Reversing near the end of a shift when fatigue is high
Visitors and new workers who do not know the rules
Soft ground and edges close to excavations
Overhead power lines when tipping

elimination: Design the site layout to separate vehicles from people and reduce reversing
substitution: Use smaller plant or one-way systems
engineering: Barriers, reversing cameras and sensors, lights, speed limiters, marked walkways
administrative: Traffic management plan, trained banksmen, authorised drivers, speed limits, visitor induction

checklist: Traffic plan briefed and up to date

legal.india: Factories Act 1948; Motor Vehicles Act 1988; BOCW Central Rules 1998 (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; client driving and site traffic rules (verify)
legal.canada: Provincial OHS regulations; Ontario Traffic Manual Book 7 for temporary road work (verify)
legal.usa: OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart O (motor vehicles, mechanized equipment); MUTCD for road work

tbt.title: Site traffic: be seen, stay out of the blind spot
points: Wear high-visibility clothing and stay on marked walkways
If you cannot see the driver, the driver cannot see you
Never walk behind reversing plant
tbt.question: Where is the nearest blind spot on our site?

activities.title: Machine Cleaning and Sanitation (Food)
activities.summary: Cleaning food processing machines with chemicals, hot water and steam.

where_first: Check the machine is isolated with lockout before any cleaning
Check the cleaning chemical label and dilution
Check floors, drains and wet areas for slip risk
Check guards are refitted before restart
hidden_hazards: Machines restarted by another person during cleaning
Mixing chlorine with acid products releases toxic gas
Hot water and steam at nozzles
Blades and slicers still moving after power off
Allergen and cross contamination from poor cleaning
protect_first: The cleaner inside or near the machine
Others who may restart the equipment

elimination: Use clean-in-place systems to avoid manual cleaning
engineering: Interlocked guards, automatic dosing, non-slip flooring, drainage
administrative: Lockout for every cleaning task, trained cleaners, chemical storage and no-mixing rule, wet floor signs
ppe: Chemical gloves, cut-resistant gloves for blades, goggles, non-slip boots, waterproof apron
Cut-resistant gloves for blades (EN 388 cut level)
checklist: Machine isolated and locked, stored energy released
No mixing of chlorine with acids
Floors and drains clear, wet floor signs out
Guards refitted and tested before restart

legal.india: Factories Act 1948; FSSAI food safety hygiene requirements; MSIHC Rules where applicable (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; municipality food control rules (for example Dubai Municipality) (verify)
legal.canada: CSA Z432 (machine safeguarding); WHMIS 2015; provincial OHS regulations

tbt.title: Cleaning machines: lock it before you wipe it
points: Your own lock on the machine before any cleaning
Never mix cleaning chemicals
Test the guards before the machine restarts
tbt.question: Who could start this machine while my hands are inside?
